text:
Seattle won 6-1, but the chances were almost dead even: 2.79 expected goals for SEA, 2.71 for CGY, and a 51-49 split in how often each side wins if you replay every shot. The scoreboard came from finishing, not from control. Calgary also had 83 shot attempts to Seattle's 53, though Seattle blocked 22 shots to Calgary's 7.

The damage came early and from modest looks. Berkly Catton scored at 2:22 of the first on a 13 percent chance, Mackie Samoskevich made it 2-0 with a backhand at 4:40, and Bobby McMann's 10 percent wrist shot made it 3-0 at 7:40. Shane Wright added a 9 percent backhand in the second, and Samoskevich scored again at 19:34 for 5-0. Dustin Wolf allowed 3.2 goals more than the 27 shots he faced deserved, which is the clearest single reason the score got away from Calgary.

Joey Daccord stopped 32 of 33 and saved 1.71 goals above expected, so he gave back little of the lead. Morgan Frost beat him on a power-play tip-in at 14:25 of the third, a 16 percent chance, but Jordan Eberle answered 39 seconds later to make it 6-1. Calgary's best miss was a 19 percent look for Mikael Backlund, off target. Brandon Montour, with two assists, was on the ice for 1.38 expected goals for and 0.46 against over 23:12.
